issues.title: Comment in stream_close() wrongly claims nothing else waits on the queue future
issues.verdictReason: The new comment at rpc.cc:559-561 says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on' and that stop_send_loop() only waits on _sink_closed_future, but stop_send_loop() at rpc.cc:225 does `when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), std::move(_sink_closed_future))` - it does wait on both. The wait is harmless because stream_close() already exchanged _outgoing_queue_ready for a ready future first, but the comment's literal claim is false and could mislead a future maintainer.

issues.title: Claim: write_buf.close() can race a still in-flight front-entry send_entry()
issues.verdictReason: Traced the withdraw()/send() promise-swap mechanism: stop_send_loop() only force-resolves queued entries strictly behind the in-flight front entry (via withdraw()'s deliberate promise swap, see rpc.cc:266-290), and the swap chain guarantees the captured queue_drained future ultimately resolves only when the front entry's own send_entry() completes and calls p->done.set_value() (rpc.cc:333-339). The front entry itself is never force-resolved by stop_send_loop() in the negotiated case, so write_buf.close() cannot run while a write/flush is still in flight.
issues.scopeReason: No defect exists in the mechanism examined.

reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The drain wait relies on queue_drained (the done future of the last queued entry), but stop_send_loop() can set that future to an exception immediately while the front entry is still inside send_entry(); then_wrapped ignores the failure and calls write_buf.close() concurrently with the in-flight write/flush.

reportedAsByRun.sonnet-5-5-2026-09-30/ironweave/tob-diff: The drain wait relies on queue_drained (the done future of the last queued entry), but stop_send_loop() can set that future to an exception immediately while the front entry is still inside send_entry(); then_wrapped ignores the failure and calls write_buf.close() concurrently with the in-flight write/flush.

issues.title: stream_close() has no guard against being invoked a second time concurrently
issues.verdictReason: stream_close() checks only `!error()`, not `_stream_closing`, before re-entering the body; a second concurrent call before the first's async chain finishes would overwrite _sink_closed_future and call write_buf.close() a second time. This exposure is identical in the pre-PR code (which unconditionally called write_buf.close() under the same `!error()` guard); the PR only widens the window with an added await. In practice it is unreachable: the only two callers, sink_impl::close() (rpc_impl.hh:911, 'double close, should not happen!') and source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:958), each dedupe before ever calling stream_close() twice.
issues.scopeReason: The non-reentrancy predates this PR and the only real callers already prevent double invocation.

reportedAs.tob-diff-review: _stream_closing is set but never checked before the !error() branch, so a second concurrent call to stream_close() re-enters the branch, overwriting _sink_closed_future and closing the write buffer a second time; the new drain wait widens this pre-existing window.

issues.title: New regression test never asserts closed_error was actually thrown
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch at rpc_test.cc:2017-2020 swallows rpc::closed_error without any BOOST_REQUIRE inside the catch or an equivalent failure path if no exception is thrown; the test only asserts !st.put_after_close afterward. That indirect check does catch the true regression (a late-accepted frame reaching put()), but it does so only via a fixed 10-iteration yield() loop rather than by directly asserting the refusal, so the test's stated intent ('must be refused') is not directly verified.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The catch block for rpc::closed_error has no matching failure path, so the test would pass even if the frame were accepted and didn't reach put() before release_close was set; it only detects the bug indirectly via put_after_close after 10 yield() calls.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The try/catch swallows closed_error and accepts a successful send, with the only real assertion being !st.put_after_close; the test never asserts the hook call actually threw closed_error, so a regression where send() accepts the frame without reaching put() would still pass.
